From 2023 to 2025, I worked across software testing, browser infrastructure, equity derivatives, commerce, and cloud infrastructure at Tarion, Mozilla, BMO Capital Markets, Shopify, and Confluent. These are my original notes on the projects, teams, and experiences from each internship, starting with the most recent.

Summer 2025

Summer @ Confluent. Data in motion. Challenging engineering.

Some of my projects included:

  • Building and designing an entire emulator system for our central infrastructure codebase. From design to implementation it was me. And I did it in a language I’ve never written (Golang + Terraform), in a role I’ve never done (Infrastructure Engineering).
  • I saved my company a projected ~$50K in cloud costs per month in just 12 weeks, with no prior use of the product itself. We cut down the CI testing by ~20 minutes with an integration with Emu (CSP Emulator)
  • I hacked AWS and Azure — I can fake authenticated users using the command line with my proxy, an interesting technical challenge.

Winter 2025

I was @ Shopify as a Software Engineering Intern working on the Product Grouping team. Did you know that bundles increase the average cart value by 50%? Product grouping is an essential part of selling strategies that Shop employs to maximize shareholder value 😀.

Some interesting things I’ve been working on:

  1. Combined listing sync job. Products can have up to 2000 variants, and combined listings work by listing a product as a variant. This means that you can actually have, 2000 x 2000 different variants total. How do you sync all the media, pricing and inventory data?
  1. Fixing exceptions with over 100k+ events with dynamic GraphQL version checking, focusing on making the merchant experience seamless. 🙏
  1. Product configuration URL regex validation. How do you verify that a URL passed in is valid? This is prevent bundles apps from containing malformed URLs for merchants that choose to create their own custom experience by making a Shopify 3p app.
  1. Fixing deadlocks. I reduced a single deadlock instance by 98% in my time there.

Fall 2024

Currently @ BMO Capital Markets as a Quantitative Developer Intern.

On the Data Cognition team doing software for equity derivatives Learning a lot about engineering and finance, really great place to be!

I worked on some pretty interesting things:

  1. Correlation between tickers using Kendal Tau. One of my biggest challenges was figuring out how to incorporate the divide and conquer method that yields a worst case runtime of O(nlogn)
  1. Options tick data API, total granular and working with a hugeeeee time series database
  1. Outlier detection for client impact scores. How do we decide that clients know more information than us when trading with us? How do we detect anomalies?

And many others.

Summer 2024

Worked at Mozilla, LOVE the team, culture and work!

I worked as a software engineer intern on the Firefox Desktop QA team.

I’m learning a lot about CI (integrations with GCP, test infrastructure, VMs and monitoring) with a dash of automation

My intern project this time is focused around monitoring infrastructure; building out integrations between our CI environment and GCP, channels of communication for receiving reports about cron jobs.

Highlights

From Mozilla, I learned the importance of simplicity in design and solutions. Although it’s tempting to implement a highly complex and advanced system with many many bells and whistles, sometimes the best decision is to keep it simple and elegant. Those are the best solutions.

Additionally, I realized the value of an amazing team and manager! They constantly uplift me and motivate me to work my hardest to push the project forward. They encourage me to take initiative and step into leadership roles even as an intern. It is really a breath of fresh air!

If you want to learn more about my technical work, feel free to reach out to me! I am more than happy to share.

Summer 2023

Worked at Tarion. Had a lot of fun as a Software Analyst Intern.

I learned a lot about software testing, developing applications for testing teams and how to identify success criteria and evaluate correctness.

My intern project was hyper focused on creating a dashboard that could be used for the QAs to quickly smoke test their applications.

Highlights

At Tarion, I learned what it really meant to be a part of a professional team and how to interact with people of all ages, not just those of my age group. It was an invaluable experience that I am so grateful for.

If you are interested in learning more about my work there on the technical side, please reach out to me!
